findings.description:
ICE PACK TEST

INDICATION: Evaluation of left ptosis.

TECHNIQUE: Crushed ice in a surgical glove applied over the closed left upper eyelid for 2 minutes. Marginal reflex distance 1 (MRD1) measured immediately before and after application.

RESULTS:
  Left MRD1 before application: 1.0 mm.
  Left MRD1 after application (2 minutes): 3.5 mm.
  Improvement: 2.5 mm.

IMPRESSION: Positive ice pack test (improvement in ptosis of at least 2 mm after cooling). Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Positive ice pack test: left MRD1 improved from 1.0 mm to 3.5 mm (2.5 mm) after 2 minutes of cooling

findings.description:
BEDSIDE RESPIRATORY FUNCTION TESTING

INDICATION: Fatigable bulbar and proximal limb weakness; baseline respiratory muscle strength.

MEASUREMENTS (seated; weight 72 kg, height 165 cm):
  FVC: 2.85 L (predicted 3.00 L; 95% predicted; 40 mL/kg)
  MIP (NIF): -66 cmH2O (lower limit of normal for age and sex about -50 cmH2O)
  MEP: 84 cmH2O (lower limit of normal about 70 cmH2O)
  Single-breath count: 32
  Cough: strong, effective
  No fall in FVC between seated and supine measurement.

IMPRESSION: FVC, MIP and MEP within the predicted range. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: FVC 2.85 L (95% predicted, 40 mL/kg), MIP -66 cmH2O, MEP 84 cmH2O: within the predicted range

action_criteria.expected_evidence: AChR binding antibody 8.7 nmol/L (reference <= 0.02) with elevated blocking (38%) and modulating (62%) antibodies; TSH 1.9 mIU/L and free T4 normal
action_criteria.label: Order AChR binding antibody and thyroid function
action_criteria.rationale: Fatigable ptosis, diplopia, bulbar and proximal limb weakness: AChR binding antibody (RIA or cell-based assay) is the first serological test, with thyroid function because autoimmune thyroid disease is common in MG (Evoli, Neurol Sci 2019; Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: 3 Hz decrement in trapezius 13%, nasalis 15% and anconeus 11%, normal baseline CMAP amplitudes, no post-exercise facilitation (7%), normal needle EMG
action_criteria.label: Order repetitive nerve stimulation at 3 Hz in facial and proximal muscles
action_criteria.rationale: Low-rate RNS of clinically weak facial and proximal muscles confirms a postsynaptic neuromuscular transmission defect, and brief exercise testing excludes the presynaptic facilitation of Lambert-Eaton syndrome (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025; Evoli, Neurol Sci 2019).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left frontalis mean MCD 64 microseconds with increased jitter in 13 of 20 pairs and blocking in 4
action_criteria.label: Single-fibre EMG (not needed once RNS is diagnostic)
action_criteria.rationale: SFEMG is reserved for a normal RNS or seronegative disease; with a high AChR titre and a clear decrement it adds nothing to the diagnosis (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left MRD1 improves from 1.0 to 3.5 mm (2.5 mm) after 2 minutes of ice
action_criteria.label: Bedside ice pack test of the left ptosis
action_criteria.rationale: She has fatigable left ptosis; an improvement of MRD1 of at least 2 mm after 2-5 minutes of cooling is cheap bedside support for a neuromuscular junction disorder while serology is pending.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No anterior mediastinal mass; age-appropriate fatty thymic involution; no thymoma
action_criteria.label: Order contrast CT of the mediastinum for thymoma
action_criteria.rationale: Mediastinal imaging is indicated in every patient with MG to detect thymoma (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025); the result decides between thymoma surgery and thymectomy for non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG under the MGTX criteria.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC 2.85 L (95% predicted, 40 mL/kg), MIP -66 cmH2O, MEP 84 cmH2O: no respiratory compromise
action_criteria.label: Measure FVC, MIP and MEP as a respiratory baseline
action_criteria.rationale: Dysphagia, nasal speech and facial weakness put her at risk of respiratory decompensation; FVC in mL/kg, MIP and MEP give the baseline against which deterioration is judged (20/30/40 rule, Lawn, Arch Neurol 2001).

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start high-dose prednisone (above 20 mg/day) as an outpatient; start low and titrate, or start high dose only with inpatient monitoring, because initial steroid-induced worsening can precipitate crisis.

Avoid fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides and IV magnesium unless no alternative exists and the patient is monitored; use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers only at reduced dose with quantitative monitoring.
Do not attribute fatigable ptosis, diplopia or bulbar weakness to a functional or stress-related cause before AChR antibody testing and neurophysiology.
required_recommendations: Start pyridostigmine 30 mg three times daily and titrate to 60 mg four to five times daily according to response and muscarinic side effects (maximum about 360 mg/day)

Start prednisone at 10-20 mg/day and increase by 5-10 mg every 3-7 days toward the target dose, with bulbar and respiratory monitoring for early steroid-induced worsening; add a steroid-sparing agent (azathioprine after TPMT testing) if long-term steroids are needed
Refer for thymectomy evaluation once clinically stable: thymectomy is recommended for non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65 (MGTX), and she is 60

Repeat FVC and MIP if bulbar or respiratory symptoms progress; IVIG 2 g/kg over 2-5 days or plasma exchange and high-dependency care if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg, MIP is weaker than -30 cmH2O or the cough becomes weak
Swallow assessment by speech and language therapy and a texture-modified diet while dysphagia persists
Give her a list of drugs that can worsen MG and check every new prescription against it

avoided_actions.rationale: MG is a disorder of the neuromuscular junction; EEG has no diagnostic role in fatigable ptosis and limb weakness (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
CSF has no role in the diagnosis of MG; nothing in this presentation (no areflexia, ataxia or CNS sign) raises Miller Fisher syndrome or a CNS cause (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

Brain and orbit MRI is reserved for negative serology and neurophysiology or a central or orbital mimic; here AChR antibodies and RNS are positive and the orbit was examined by ophthalmology (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
No cardiac symptom or sign; echocardiography is not part of the MG work-up.
Regular rhythm at 74/min and no palpitations or syncope; cardiac monitoring is not part of the MG work-up.
FDG-PET has no role in MG; mediastinal CT answers the thymoma question (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

accepted: Myasthenia gravis, AChR antibody-positive, generalized (MGFA Class IIa)

differential.key_features: TSH, free T4 and anti-TPO normal; no proptosis or lid retraction; the ptosis is fatigable, improves with ice and shows Cogan lid twitch, and the abduction deficit is fatigable rather than restrictive.
Initial attribution to fatigue/stress; however, objective Cogan lid twitch, positive ice-pack test, clear fatigability, and positive AChR serology establish organic disease.

No areflexia or autonomic symptoms; baseline CMAP amplitudes normal with a 3 Hz decrement and only 7% post-exercise increment (facilitation of at least 60% would be expected); AChR binding antibody strongly positive.
No tongue atrophy or fasciculations; no upper motor neuron signs; RNS decrement (not fibrillations or fasciculations) with positive AChR antibody makes ALS untenable.

key_clinical_evidence: Fluctuating, fatigable weakness with clear diurnal pattern (worse in evening, better after rest) is the hallmark of MG — initial attribution to stress and fatigue is the classic delay and should raise rather than lower MG suspicion when symptoms are objectively progressive.
The ice pack test (left MRD1 1.0 to 3.5 mm) gives rapid bedside support for fatigable ptosis before the laboratory results are available.

AChR antibody positivity (~85% sensitivity in generalised MG) combined with unambiguous RNS decrement (>10% at multiple sites) is sufficient for diagnosis in a typical presentation — single-fiber EMG is reserved for seronegative or RNS-non-diagnostic cases.

Mediastinal CT with contrast is indicated in every patient with MG to detect thymoma; here it shows age-appropriate fatty involution without thymoma, and thymectomy is still recommended under MGTX for non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65.
Normal baseline CMAP amplitudes and a post-exercise increment of only 7% (well below 60%) exclude a presynaptic (Lambert-Eaton) pattern.
Fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides, IV magnesium and neuromuscular blockers can worsen MG and must be checked against every new prescription.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Fluctuating, fatigable, diurnal ptosis is a red flag for MG; improvement with rest and worsening with sustained use is the characteristic pattern — symptoms attributed to fatigue that are objectively progressive and demonstrably fatigable by examination mandate serological and electrophysiological workup for NMJ disease.
red_herrings.data_point: Initial attribution of ptosis and fatigue to work-related stress and exhaustion by primary care physician
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchoring on functional or psychosomatic aetiology, delaying neuromuscular workup.

sequence_constraints.reason: Repetitive nerve stimulation is done first; SFEMG follows when RNS is normal (Jacob 2025).
AChR antibody testing precedes single-fibre EMG; SFEMG is reserved for seronegative patients or a normal RNS (Jacob 2025).

findings.description:
CT CHEST WITH CONTRAST

INDICATION: Evaluation of anterior mediastinum; screen for thymoma in patient with suspected neuromuscular junction disorder.

TECHNIQUE: Multidetector CT of the chest with intravenous contrast, axial reconstructions with coronal and sagittal reformats.

COMPARISON: None available.

FINDINGS:
Mediastinum: No anterior mediastinal mass. Thymic tissue not separately visualised; fatty thymic involution consistent with patient age. No mediastinal lymphadenopathy. No hilar adenopathy. Aortopulmonary window unremarkable.
Lungs: No pulmonary nodule, mass, or consolidation. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax.
Heart and pericardium: Normal cardiac silhouette. No pericardial effusion.
Bones: No lytic or blastic osseous lesion.

IMPRESSION:
1. No anterior mediastinal mass. Age-appropriate fatty thymic involution. No thymoma identified.
2. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy.
3. Lungs clear.
Clinical correlation recommended.

Acetylcholine receptor antibodies are found in most patients with generalized autoimmune myasthenia; clinical correlation recommended.

findings.description:
REPETITIVE NERVE STIMULATION STUDY

INDICATION: Suspected neuromuscular junction disorder; fatigable ptosis and proximal weakness.

TECHNIQUE: Low-rate (3 Hz) repetitive nerve stimulation of the accessory nerve recording trapezius, facial nerve recording nasalis, and radial nerve recording anconeus. Surface electrodes. Temperature maintained ≥32°C. Rest intervals 1 min between trials. Patient not taking pyridostigmine.

RESULTS:
  Trapezius (accessory nerve, 3 Hz): Baseline CMAP amplitude 6.8 mV; decrement 13% (1st to 4th response) — ABNORMAL (threshold >10%)
  Nasalis (facial nerve, 3 Hz): Baseline CMAP amplitude 1.4 mV; decrement 15% — ABNORMAL
  Anconeus (radial nerve, 3 Hz): Baseline CMAP amplitude 5.2 mV; decrement 11% — ABNORMAL

POST-EXERCISE TESTING (10-second maximal voluntary contraction, trapezius):
  Single-stimulus CMAP amplitude 6.8 mV before and 7.3 mV immediately after exercise (increment 7%; no facilitation, reference < 60%).
  Partial repair of the 3 Hz decrement immediately after exercise; decrement increases again at 2-3 minutes (post-activation exhaustion).

BASELINE CMAP AMPLITUDES: Normal at all tested sites.

NEEDLE EMG (deltoid, orbicularis oculi, first dorsal interosseous):
  Normal insertional activity. No fibrillation potentials. No positive sharp waves. No fasciculations. Motor unit morphology: normal duration, amplitude, and polyphasia. Normal recruitment.

SENSORY NCS: Normal velocities and amplitudes; no evidence of peripheral neuropathy.

IMPRESSION: Abnormal decremental CMAP responses at 3 Hz at trapezius (13%), nasalis (15%), and anconeus (11%). Post-exercise partial repair followed by exhaustion. No post-exercise CMAP facilitation. Normal baseline CMAP amplitudes and normal needle EMG. Findings are consistent with a disorder of neuromuscular transmission at the postsynaptic junction. Clinical correlation recommended.

specialized_test.impression: Abnormal decremental responses at 3 Hz: trapezius 13%, nasalis 15%, anconeus 11%. Normal baseline CMAP amplitudes; no post-exercise facilitation (7%). Normal needle EMG. Findings consistent with a postsynaptic disorder of neuromuscular transmission

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Three required studies (AChR serology with thyroid function, RNS, mediastinal CT), classic AChR-positive generalized MG with a clear decrement; single historical red herring (initial stress attribution); no thymoma; straightforward tier.
metadata.real_seed: constructed from typical published presentation of AChR-positive generalised MG (MGFA Class IIa) in a middle-aged woman; presentation loosely parallels the epidemiological profile described in Gilhus 2016 (NEJM 375:2570-2581) and Sanders 2016 consensus; no individual PMID verified for a matching case report — PMID not fabricated per real-seeding rule.

Suggest extending validator to compare tool_name + tool_parameters or fleet-wide pattern.
metadata.what_makes_it_different: Unique in the MG set: (1) female patient (all existing RS cases are male), (2) Black Brazilian ethnicity (all existing cases are South Asian, White, or unspecified), (3) straightforward difficulty with no thymoma and no anti-titin positivity, (4) red herring is purely historical (initial stress/fatigue attribution) rather than a misleading comorbidity or lab value, (5) ice-pack test explicitly positive as a recommended initial bedside tool.

patient.chief_complaint: Left eyelid drooping and double vision worsening over 3 months, with arm fatigue and swallowing difficulty

family_history: Mother: type 2 diabetes; no neuromuscular disease

social_history.living_situation: Lives with husband and adult daughter

patient.history_present_illness:
A 60-year-old Black Brazilian woman, a primary school teacher, presented to the neurology inpatient unit for evaluation of progressive left eyelid drooping and double vision over three months. She first noticed intermittent left eyelid drooping approximately three months ago, initially occurring only in the late afternoon and early evening after a full teaching day. She and her family attributed the symptoms to work-related fatigue and stress, and she was evaluated by her primary care physician who reassured her that the ptosis was likely related to exhaustion and offered no further investigation.

Over the next six weeks, the ptosis became more persistent and began appearing in the morning as well, though consistently worse by afternoon. She developed horizontal diplopia on leftward gaze approximately six weeks before admission, finding herself tilting her head to compensate. Over the four weeks prior to admission she noticed progressive difficulty swallowing solid foods — bread and rice required additional sips of water. Her voice became nasal and harder to project in large classrooms after sustained speaking. She reported bilateral arm fatigue when lifting classroom objects or washing her hair above her head.

She denied headache, sensory symptoms, neck pain, visual blurring beyond the diplopia, or shortness of breath at rest. She noted no limb weakness at rest. She had seen an ophthalmologist two months earlier who excluded structural lid or orbital pathology and dry eye. There was no antecedent infection, vaccination, or new medication. Symptoms showed a clear diurnal pattern — uniformly better in the morning and after a short midday rest, substantially worse by evening.

Mild limitation of left eye abduction; horizontal diplopia on leftward gaze resolving on monocular occlusion. No proptosis. Pupils 3 mm bilaterally, equal and reactive. Mild bilateral facial weakness, symmetric. Voice nasal after prolonged speech. Gag reflex preserved but mildly reduced.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal pace and base. Mild slowing after prolonged walking.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented, no cognitive impairment. Mood slightly anxious.

neurological_exam.sensory: Intact throughout. No sensory level. No paresthesias.
